steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Star hopping uses easily recognisable patterns (like the Plough) to locate fainter objects

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A planisphere is a rotating star map that shows which constellations are visible at a given date and time

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Angular separation can be estimated using hand measurements: little finger at arm's length ≈ 1°, fist ≈ 10°

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Seeing conditions depend on atmospheric turbulence, light pollution and transparency

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is star hopping? | Q: How can you estimate angular separation without equipment? | Q: What factors affect seeing conditions?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A technique for finding faint objects by starting at a bright, recognisable star pattern and moving in steps using nearby stars until the target is reached. | Using hand measurements at arm's length: little finger ≈ 1°, three middle fingers ≈ 5°, fist ≈ 10°, outstretched hand span ≈ 20°. | Atmospheric turbulence (causing twinkling/scintillation), light pollution, cloud cover, humidity and air transparency.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Hand-angle measurements are specifically on the Edexcel specification Both boards require understanding of how to use a planisphere Seeing vs transparency: seeing = steadiness of atmosphere; transparency = clarity/brightness Transit and occultation: transit = small in front of big; occultation = big hides small
